newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EDP to pay extraordinary dividend for '97.
newsitem.headline: EDP to pay extraordinary dividend for '97.

text.p: State utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, due to be partially privatised next month, expects to pay an extraordinary dividend of 10 billion escudos in 1997, according to the prospectus of the public offer to sell (OPV).
The extraordinary dividend would supplement a "dividend payout" of 65 percent for 1997 results, already guaranteed by EDP president Antonio de Almeida. The dividend payout was 69 percent in 1996.
Analysts have forecast that EDP will make a consolidated net profit of between 90 and 100 billion escudos in 1997. The company has made no forecasts.
In 1996, Portugal's dominant electricity generator and distributor posted a consolidated net profit of 81.145 billion escudos.
In the first quarter of 1997, consolidated net profit rose 21 percent, compared with the first quarter of 1996, to 29.16 billion escudos.

According to sources close to the privatisation, applications in the OPV stood at more than one billion EDP shares, which means that demand in the OPV was expected to outstrip supply by more than 10 times.
The Portuguese government is expected to privatise some 25 percent of EDP's capital in a special session to be held on Lisbon bourse on June 16.
